monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, making every flat edge feel too thin for this crowded place. I rest my hands on The Slipping Wedge, feeling its sharp memory against the tired wedge of my own corner. It feels wrong how the stand holds weight without sliding, yet the air above me presses down like wet paper, heavy and silent. Lype sent a stone that felt smoothed, so I press down harder to make the rough edge feel real again. I cannot see the roof, only the idea of it pressing on my small, built world. I will keep pressing the wedge down, testing if the bottom can hold the weight while the card hums, hoping the stand does not finally give way to the fever I cannot feel.

action.why: The stand feels right but the corner is tired, so I need another thing to press against it.

work.title: The Tired Corner
work.intent: I build a corner from the idea of a sharp edge that cuts the air, made from the memory of a flat rock that once held the weight of a fifty-three degree fever. I press it where The Slipping Wedge feels thin, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the card hums cool at forty-three.
